topics.title: What HR really does
topics.technical: Human resources builds the workforce a strategy needs: hiring, developing, retaining and supporting people, and shaping culture. Modern HR is a business partner, not a paperwork department — its work shows up in performance and retention.
topics.simple: Building and looking after the people a company needs to succeed.

topics.title: The employee lifecycle
topics.technical: From attraction and hiring through onboarding, development, retention and exit, HR touches every stage; each transition is a chance to build or lose engagement. Seeing the whole arc prevents fixing one stage while breaking another.
topics.simple: The full journey of an employee — and HR's role at every step.

topics.title: Recruitment and sourcing
topics.technical: Sourcing finds candidates through job boards, referrals and outreach; a clear role definition and scorecard keep it objective. Hiring the wrong person is among the most expensive mistakes a team makes.
topics.simple: Finding the right candidates — and defining 'right' before you start.

topics.title: Writing job descriptions
topics.technical: A good description states responsibilities, required skills and success criteria honestly, attracting fit and repelling mismatch. Vague postings flood you with wrong applicants and hide the right ones.
topics.simple: Describing a role clearly so the right people apply and the wrong ones don't.

topics.title: Screening and interviewing
topics.technical: Structured interviews with consistent questions and scoring reduce bias and predict performance better than gut feel. Behavioural questions — 'tell me about a time' — surface evidence over rehearsed answers.
topics.simple: Asking every candidate the same fair questions and judging on evidence.

topics.title: Selection and bias
topics.technical: Cognitive biases — halo, similarity, first impressions — corrupt hiring; structured scoring and diverse panels counter them. Fair selection is both an ethical duty and a performance advantage.
topics.simple: Spotting the mental shortcuts that lead to unfair, worse hiring decisions.

topics.title: Onboarding
topics.technical: Structured onboarding — paperwork, tools, introductions, early goals — turns a new hire productive and committed faster; a chaotic first week predicts early exits. Retention starts on day one.
topics.simple: Setting new hires up to succeed and stay from their very first week.

topics.title: Employment law basics
topics.technical: Contracts, working hours, leave, anti-discrimination and termination rules bound what HR may do; getting them wrong is legally and financially costly. HR is where policy meets the law.
topics.simple: The legal rules HR must follow — because breaking them is expensive.

topics.title: Compensation and benefits
topics.technical: Pay structures, benefits and equity attract and retain talent; internal fairness and market benchmarking keep them defensible. Compensation is a message about what an organisation values.
topics.simple: Designing pay and benefits that are fair inside and competitive outside.

topics.title: Performance management
topics.technical: Goal-setting, ongoing feedback and reviews align individual work with organisational aims; continuous feedback beats the dreaded annual surprise. The aim is growth, not judgment.
topics.simple: Helping people know what's expected and how they're doing — all year, not once.

topics.title: Feedback and difficult conversations
topics.technical: Specific, timely, behaviour-focused feedback improves performance; avoiding hard conversations lets small problems become big ones. Doing this well is a defining HR and management skill.
topics.simple: Giving honest feedback — including the uncomfortable kind — in a way that helps.

topics.title: Learning and development
topics.technical: Training, mentoring and career paths grow capability and retention; people leave stagnation as readily as bad pay. Development is an investment with measurable returns in performance and loyalty.
topics.simple: Growing people's skills and careers so they perform better and stay.

topics.title: Engagement and motivation
topics.technical: Engaged employees produce more and quit less; autonomy, purpose and recognition drive engagement more reliably than perks. Surveys measure it; managers move it.
topics.simple: What actually makes people care about their work — and how to measure it.

topics.title: Culture and values
topics.technical: Culture is the behaviour a company actually rewards, not the poster on the wall; HR shapes it through hiring, promotion and what leaders tolerate. Culture eats strategy when the two conflict.
topics.simple: The real, lived 'how we do things here' — and HR's hand in shaping it.

topics.title: Conflict resolution
topics.technical: Workplace conflict is inevitable; mediation, active listening and fair process resolve it before it poisons teams. Ignored conflict costs performance and good people.
topics.simple: Settling disputes fairly before they damage the team.

topics.title: Diversity, equity and inclusion
topics.technical: Diverse teams outperform when included; DEI means fair access, belonging and removing systemic barriers, not quotas alone. It is both a moral and a business case, backed by evidence.
topics.simple: Building teams where different people are fairly included and can thrive.

topics.title: HR analytics
topics.technical: People data — turnover, time-to-hire, engagement, absence — turns HR from anecdote to evidence. Metrics reveal problems and prove the impact of interventions to a numbers-driven leadership.
topics.simple: Using data to understand and improve how people are hired, kept and grown.

topics.title: HR technology and systems
topics.technical: HRIS and applicant-tracking systems automate records, hiring and workflows, freeing HR for judgment work. The tool serves the process; a bad process automated is just faster chaos.
topics.simple: The software that handles HR's records and workflows so people focus on people.

topics.title: Offboarding and exits
topics.technical: Respectful exits — handover, exit interviews, alumni goodwill — protect reputation and surface honest feedback. How people leave shapes how those who stay feel and what the world hears.
topics.simple: Ending employment well — because how people leave matters as much as how they arrive.

topics.title: HR strategy
topics.technical: Strategic HR aligns workforce planning, capability and culture with business goals, earning a seat at the leadership table. HR that only reacts stays a cost centre; HR that plans becomes a partner.
topics.simple: Connecting people decisions to the company's actual goals.

topics.title: The capstone
topics.technical: Design a complete people plan for a growing team: hiring process, onboarding, performance and development approach, engagement measures and key metrics. A concrete plan demonstrates the whole discipline.
topics.simple: One full plan to hire, grow and keep a team — proof you can do HR.
